angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,335,744 km at 149.59 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.6850 +/- 0.0186 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 149.59 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.92 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1431 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..292A/abstract): 1,335,744 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.9 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1431 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..292A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 7690 +/- 400 K from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1431 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..292A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Addison et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1431 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..292A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1431.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.150, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
